findings.text: The change locked the CLI's ingest cadence at sixty seconds but left the module's own second entry point disagreeing with it. imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_ingest.py still defines DEFAULT_CADENCE_SECONDS = 5.0 (line 59), still defaults run() to it (line 179), and still exposes main() (line 259) whose argparse --cadence reads that same 5.0 (line 248), with its docstring calling itself 'the scheduled ingest' and 'the entry point the scheduled job runs' (lines 260-262). Reproduced: at the reviewed head, `python -m imas_ambix.agent.telemetry_ingest --help` prints '--cadence CADENCE  seconds between ticks (default: 5.0)' while `imas-ambix agent ingest --help` prints '[default: 60.0]'. This is the same class of hazard 5 names as the reason for removing --submit and --dry-run ('a second, unused placement invites the wrong deploy'): a second runnable ingest path carries the pre-decision five-second cadence, so a caller -- or the supervisor, if it ever reaches the module entry point rather than the CLI at a future change -- ticks at 5 s against the 60 s the lead locked. Nothing invokes main() in-repo, and the reviewed run's own manifest acknowledged the residual ('telemetry_ingest.DEFAULT_CADENCE_SECONDS remains 5.0 (library default, not in this node's scope)'), so this is recorded as a residual of the node's goal rather than a defect the commit introduced.

follow_ons.text: The landed evidence fragment srw-ingest-command-and-service.html still documents generate_ingest_script and `agent ingest --dry-run` as the ingest's SLURM service. That fragment is an immutable landed record of the node that added the generator, so it is not this commit's to edit and no finding is raised against it; it is recorded so the plan's fragment set is not read as describing an option that now raises 'no such option'. A reader wanting the current placement should read 5's own text and the CLI help.
